II.4 1380b35-1381a1.text: We may describe friendly feeling towards any one as wishing for him what you believe to be good things, not for your own sake but for his, and being inclined, so far as you can, to bring these things about. (W. Rhys Roberts) | 'Let loving [to philein] be wishing for someone the things that he deems good, for the sake of that person and not oneself, and the accomplishment of these things to the best of one's ability.' (tr. D. Konstan)
II.4 1380b35-1381a1.notes: Aquinas's 'amare est velle alicui bonum' is a compressed Latin form of this; Aristotle's full definition adds 'for his sake, not one's own' and 'to bring it about'.
